questions: Do line_loss_events fall from 1 per run to 0 with the ±4 cm span at 4 cm lead?
Does s-bend progress stay at or above 0.155, and does oval progress stay at or above 0.11?
Is max_error below 0.06 m, and at what progress does each run still end (if it ends)?
Does steering_oscillation stay within 0.07 to 0.15 with the 2 cm pitch?
Does rms_error stay near 0.03 on all tracks? If so, the offset is probably a motor-mismatch term, and the next lever is the controller (ki or kd), not geometry.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line losses fall to 0 but progress stays below 0.15 on the s-bend, tell me whether kp or kd needs raising to use the wider span. If line losses are still 1 and progress is unchanged, tell me whether a line_loss setting change (last_direction versus search) would reduce the loss.

intent: Single-variable test from iteration 4 (the ±3 cm, 16 mm, 4 cm lead design). Widen the five-sensor span from ±3 cm to ±4 cm at a 2 cm pitch, keeping the 4 cm lead, 16 mm footprints, 0.6 kg mass, 0.11 m track and 0.03 m wheel radius. The goal is to remove the one line loss per run that the ±3 cm span leaves, without the short-lead penalty that confounded iteration 2. Expect line_loss_events near 0, progress at or above 0.15 on the s-bend and at or above 0.11 on the oval, and max_error below 0.06 m.
learning: Iteration 4 (16 mm, ±3 cm, 4 cm lead) gave s-bend progress 0.155, oval 0.11, slalom 0.1075, and 1 line loss per run, matching iteration 1. So sensor_size is not a lever at 4 cm lead. The remaining geometry question is whether the outer sensors at ±3 cm are too close to the line on bends. Iteration 2 mixed a ±6 cm span with a 3 cm lead, so its progress drop cannot be assigned to span alone. The ±4 cm test separates the two. Measure line_loss_events, progress, max_error and steering_oscillation on all three development tracks.
rationale: Iteration 4 (±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 16 mm footprints) scored 51.12, essentially level with iteration 1 (51.27). The s-bend progress was 0.155 in both, and line_loss_events stayed at 1 per run. So the footprint change did nothing measurable, and sensor_size 0.016 is neutral. The rule I set last iteration now applies: progress is unchanged and line losses remain at 1, so the next geometry test is a ±4 cm span at 16 mm with 5 sensors. Iteration 2's s-bend collapse (progress 0.04) came with a 3 cm lead as well as the ±6 cm span. Iteration 3 showed a short lead is harmful, so that collapse is not clean evidence against a wider span at a 4 cm lead. I therefore keep the 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius and 0.12 m body, and change only the span: x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 at y = 0.04 m, with sensor_size 0.016 m. Expected result: the outermost sensors reach the tape on bends that currently drop one line loss per run, so line_loss_events should fall toward 0 and max_error should stay below about 0.06 m. Progress should hold at or above 0.15 on the s-bend. If progress falls below 0.11 on the oval, the span is too wide and I return to ±3 cm. The steady rms_error of about 0.03 on every track is probably a motor-mismatch offset, which is a controller question for the Integrator, not something geometry can fix.
